events.quote: ask with Can I have or Could I have, and add please
Right: Could I have a cake, please? Wrong: Give me a cake.

next_task.correct: Could I have a coffee, please?

events.quote: use an before the sounds a, e, i, o or u, and a before other sounds
Right: He has an owl. Wrong: He has a owl.
We use at with clock times (at 7 o'clock), on with days (on Monday) and in with months (in July)
Instead of Give me, we say Can I have ... please?

next_task.correct: Can I have a coffee, please?

events.quote: Use many with things you can count and much with things you cannot count.
Right: How much water is in the cup? Wrong: How many water is in the cup?
start a sentence with a capital letter, write I as a capital letter, and end with a full stop
Request with Could I have ... or I would like ..., and add please.
Right: Can I have a juice, please? Wrong: Give me a juice.

next_task.correct: Could I have a coffee, please?

events.quote: say who first, then the action, then the thing, and put time or place last
Right: Tom drinks milk at home. Wrong: Drinks Tom milk at home.
Use am with I, is with he, she and it, and are with you, we and they.
Some past verbs are irregular. They change in special ways, like go -> went and buy -> bought.
we use did + subject + base verb, and the main verb does not change
For past questions we use did + subject + base verb

next_task.correct: Did you go to the beach yesterday?

errors.W1: Did you went to the beach yesterday?

events.quote: "a" goes before a consonant sound (a pen) and "an" goes before a vowel sound (an apple)

next_task.correct: the last time they agree on

events.quote: start a sentence with a capital letter and end it with a full stop
Right: The bus is late. Wrong: the bus is late
Every sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop.
put the subject first, then the verb, then the object, then place or time
Right: Tom reads a map at home. Wrong: Reads Tom a map at home.
Use a before a consonant sound and an before a vowel sound.
Right: I see an egg. Wrong: I see a egg.
We use am/is/are + going to + verb for plans.

next_task.correct: I am going to study tonight.

events.quote: Adverbs like always, usually, sometimes and never go before the main verb.

next_task.correct: Did you go to the cinema last weekend?

errors.W1: Did you went to the cinema last weekend?
errors.W2: You went to the cinema last weekend?

events.quote: begin a sentence with a capital letter and end it with a full stop
Right: Our dog barks. Wrong: our dog barks
We use some in positive sentences (I have some tea) and any in questions and negatives
Some common verbs have a special past form, so we do not add -ed.
Right: He drank water yesterday. Wrong: He drinked water yesterday.
